title: A NASA Plane Spotted Topaz in the Mojave Without Touching the Ground
description:
How did NASA find topaz in the Mojave Desert from a plane? NASA's ER-2 flies at about 65,000 feet with AVIRIS, an imaging spectrometer that reads the light fingerprint of minerals pixel by pixel. In the GEMx project with the U.S. Geological Survey, it spotted a topaz signature on a ridge near Barstow, California, and geologists confirmed it on foot. Topaz can point to porphyry copper, and the same survey found hectorite, a lithium-bearing clay, in old mine waste.

In this episode:

0:17 NASA's ER-2 at 65,000 feet
0:35 AVIRIS and the light fingerprint of minerals
1:08 GEMx and America's critical minerals
1:39 The topaz signal near Barstow
1:56 Why topaz could point to copper
2:13 Lithium clay and the Colorado flights
